Frontend UI verified: super_admin sees all 17 tabs, Cotizaciones CTA prominent, permissions modal with 17 feature toggles works, AdminPackages visibility filter (Todos/Public/Internal) + form visibility field work, AdminQuotations date/creator filters live-filter the list and rows display creator name ('por Super Admin' / 'por Sistema (web pública)').

minor.issue: Review spec referenced PUT /api/admin/users/{user_id} for updating permissions, but the actual implemented route is PUT /api/admin/users/{user_id}/permissions. The frontend AdminUsers page uses the /permissions subpath correctly, so no functional break. Consider aligning docs.

Admin without ?include_internal=true still gets the public-only filter (visibility=public OR missing). Management panels must pass include_internal=true explicitly. Verified AdminPackages.js does so. Note for future: may be clearer to default admin requests to include internal.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~2729 lines; still over the 700-line threshold. Router split (auth/admin_users/packages/quotations) remains recommended.

FEATURE_KEYS is a hardcoded Python list on backend and mirrored in AdminUsers.js. If a new feature/tab is added, both must be updated. Consider exposing a single source via GET /api/admin/feature-keys (already exists) and letting AdminUsers.js render from that response instead of duplicating the list.

AdminDashboard permission gating: `hasPerm = role==='super_admin' || !permissions || Object.keys(perms).length===0 || !!perms[key]`. The Object.keys().length===0 fallback means any admin with empty perms sees ALL tabs — this masks the feature. Decide whether empty-perms should mean 'no access' or 'legacy-all-access' and document. Currently documented as legacy fallback which is fine.

POST /api/admin/users defaults new 'admin' role to {dashboard, quotations, clients} if perms omitted. UI creation form does not pass permissions on create, so newly created admins can only see 3 tabs until super_admin edits them. Verify that UX is intended.

GET /api/quotations date filter uses string comparison with ISO timestamps. date_to appends 'T23:59:59' but date_from doesn't, so an item at exactly 'YYYY-MM-DD' with T00:00:00 is included — correct. However, comparing strings is tz-naive; if created_at stores +00:00 explicitly it would still lexically sort, but worth a unit test if timezones vary.

GET /api/packages admin path: even super_admin must pass include_internal=true to see internal items. If AdminPackages page is ever loaded without this flag, internal packages would be hidden from management — fragile. Consider defaulting include_internal=true when the caller is admin.
